subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw core add a public dreaming provider protocol for memory plugins, or keep dreaming orchestration plugin-owned while only documenting ClawHub/community implementations?
rationale: The request would add public plugin/config/runtime surface and decide ownership of scheduling, phase orchestration, storage callbacks, and UI/command behavior; source inspection shows this is not a narrow broken-contract bug.

options.title: Design the core SDK protocol
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical tracker and design the dreaming provider contract together with memory role-slot decisions before implementation.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub plugins
options.body: Document that alternative memory backends should ship their own dreaming implementations on ClawHub and close this only after maintainers explicitly reject a core protocol.

options.title: Wait for role-slot landing
options.body: Pause implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 lands or closes, then revisit whether memory.dreaming needs a deeper provider interface.

recommendation.title: Design the core SDK protocol
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical tracker and design the dreaming provider contract together with memory role-slot decisions before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vignesh introduced the memory-core dreaming runtime that would be split or generalized by this decision.
